title: Harness file-tool scope is permanently bound to launch worktree; in-session `git worktree add` produces an unreachable dir
wanted_capability: File-mutation and read tools (`file_read`, `file_edit`, `file_write`, `code.*`, `analysis.*`, `java.*`) can operate in a worktree other than the session's `launch_root`. Today, `git worktree add <somewhere>` from within a session leaves `<somewhere>` stranded — every standard tool returns `path escapes worktree root`, and the only operator workaround is to spawn a fresh dispatch.
missing_primitive: A session-scoped `sandbox_worktree_enter` / `sandbox_set_root` primitive that re-binds the file-mutation and read scopes (file_read/edit/write, code.*, analysis.*, java.*) to a different worktree path. Currently `sandbox_status(root=…)` only inspects, it doesn't switch.
fallback_used: Stopped and asked the operator to choose between (1) branch-in-main-worktree (loses disk isolation) and (2) spawn a fresh sub-agent in the new worktree (heavyweight for a small fix). Operator picked (1).
notes: The on-disk worktree is stranded but visible to `sandbox_status` and `git worktree list`. The harness's `launch_root` is permanent for the session. The 'fresh starting place' is achievable on a new branch in the main worktree, but the operator's "new worktree" framing implies a separate disk directory, which the tool surface can't reach. Either the tool surface needs a switch primitive, or the operator-facing language ("worktree" vs "branch") needs a sharp distinction in the daily-cleaning / closeout docs.
resolution_note: Addressed by dropping the lexical-containment check in `bro_tools::workspace::resolve_in_root` and `bro_apply_patch::apply::resolve_within`. File tools (`file_read`/`file_edit`/`file_write`/`code.*`/`analysis.*`/`java.*`/apply-patch) now accept absolute paths; relative paths still join against the effective worktree root. Schema descriptions updated to say so. The `path escapes worktree root` denial is gone. The harness had no other sandboxing machinery — shell already escaped any `cx.root` boundary with `git -C`, `find`, `tee`, `sed -i`, etc. — so the structured-tool confinement was a speed bump, not a boundary (friction/2026-June-13-0840pm-worktree-containment-issues.md). LSP refactor plan safety checks (`lsp_facts.rs::WorkspaceEdit` and `java_transforms.rs::refactor_plan`) intentionally retained: those are refactor plan integrity checks, not file-tool confinement.
